interest: Illuminates SCAP's transition from emergency postwar coal management to aggressive mine mechanization, rationalization, and American technical advising.
overview: This file documents the rehabilitation, administration, and technical modernization of Japan's coal mining industry under the Allied Occupation between November 1945 and November 1949. Initial records focus on acute postwar production crises, labor and material shortages, emergency regional allocations to South Korea, the establishment of the Japanese Coal Board, and parliamentary debates over coal regulation. Subsequent State Department and SCAP records detail efforts to overcome labor unrest, survey Hokkaido coal fields, and accelerate mine mechanization to reach ambitious production quotas, culminating in the 1949 drive to achieve 42 million metric tons without state subsidies under the Nine-Point Economic Stabilization Program. The file also chronicles American engineering surveys, bilateral technical study tours, geological exploration assessments, and investigations into domestic metallurgical coking coal self-sufficiency.
